title: Effect of classical noises on the coherent population trapping based on the Green's function approach to the multiplicative stochastic processes
authors: M. Mirzaee, B. Askari, Ali Motazedifard, A. Dalafi
abstract: Inspired by the Green's function (GF) approach in quantum field theory (QFT) and many body physics, we have developed a mathematical formalism to investigate classical multiplicative stochastic processes. Based on this approach, the interacting GF of any dynamical system subjected to classical stochastic noises, which enter into the system equations of motion in a multiplicative way, can be obtained from the noninteracting (free of noise) GF through an infinite perturbative series which may converge to an exact closed form under special conditions. Using this formalism, we have studied the effects of classical noises of the driving laser on the coherent population trapping (CPT) which have a crucial role in the performance of CPT-based atomic clocks. We have shown that if the bandwidth of the colored noise is sufficiently larger than the system damping rate, the infinite series corresponding to the interacting GF can be approximated by the closed form. The presented formalism enables us to investigate all kinds of homogeneous and inhomogeneous broadening mechanisms on the CPT transmission resonance lineshape, including dephasing due to atomic collisions, power/Doppler broadenings, as well as the broadening mechanisms due to phase and amplitude fluctuations of driving laser and compared their destructive effect with each other. It should be emphasized that the presented formalism is applicable to any dynamical system with multiplicative stochastic noises and the CPT phenomenon is just a prototype for the application of the presented formalism in practice.
summary: The paper develops an advanced mathematical formalism using the Green's function approach to analyze open quantum systems subjected to classical multiplicative stochastic noises. It applies this theory to Coherent Population Trapping (CPT) in atomic clocks, demonstrating how noise from laser fluctuations and collisions broaden the resonance line shape. This provides a general framework applicable to any system with such noise sources.
main_problem: The study investigates how classical multiplicative stochastic noises affect Coherent Population Trapping (CPT), a phenomenon vital for high-precision atomic clocks.
main_result: A generalized Green's function formalism is developed that allows the calculation of system dynamics under colored noise, providing insights into how various broadening mechanisms destructively interact on the CPT resonance line shape.
method: The core method involves extending the Green's function approach from QFT to solve stochastic differential equations (SDEs) describing the noisy quantum evolution via infinite perturbative series approximations.
model_or_system: The system is an atomic ensemble exhibiting CPT in a $\Lambda$-scheme, driven by two coherent laser fields. The dynamics are modeled using multiplicative SDEs incorporating noise from laser phase and amplitude fluctuations, alongside standard broadening mechanisms like Doppler shifts and collisions.
key_observables: CPT transmission resonance line shape (width, height, contrast); the interacting Green's function $\langle G(t) angle$.
important_parameters: Noise bandwidth relative to system damping rate; correlation time scales of the colored noise ($\kappa$ vs. $\gamma$).
main_assumptions: The formalism assumes that for multiplicative colored noises, an approximation by a closed form is valid when the noise bandwidth significantly exceeds the system damping rate.
figures_summary: Figure 1 schematically illustrates the experimental setup involving a laser source interacting with an atomic vapor cell to measure CPT.
paper_structure: The paper introduces the general GF formalism for multiplicative stochastic processes, applies it to the specific case of CPT dynamics governed by master equations derived from SDEs, and then analyzes the resulting power spectra under different noise assumptions (white vs. colored).
why_interesting: This work provides a powerful, generalized theoretical tool—the Green's function approach for multiplicative noise—that moves beyond simpler white-noise approximations to model realistic decoherence sources in quantum optics experiments.

figures.caption: FIG. 1. Schematic representation of the experimental setup for detection of the CPT transmission resonance line when a gas of alkali-metal atoms are subjected to the radiation of two beams extracted from the same laser source so that the atomic levels form a Λ-shape structure. The excited level |3⟩of each interacting atom has the spontaneous emission rates of Γ31 and Γ32 to the hyperfine ground state levels |1⟩and |2⟩while the |1⟩→|2⟩transition is dipole forbidden. The two coupling and probe beams with frequencies ωc and ωp are counterpropagating in order to neutralize the Doppler broadening as much as possible.

FIG. 2. Feynman diagram representation of the infinite series expansion of the interacting (noisy) GF. The interacting GF is demonstrated by the directional double line on the left hand side, while the noninteracting (noiseless) GF is represented by directional single lines and the self-energy contribution by solid black circles on the right hand side. The diagrams illustrate the repeated interaction processes appearing in the perturbative expansion of Eq.(40).

FIG. 3. Time evolution of the populations of energy levels as well as the coherence between ground state hyperfine levels in the absence of noises and broadening mechanisms with the initial condition where the atom is its ground state assuming γ12 = 0. The lasers parameters have been considered as Ωc = Ωp = 0.4γ, ∆c = 0, and δ = 0.

FIG. 4. (Color online) (a) Time evolution of ρ33(γt), and (b) time evolution of ρ12(γt), at δ = 0 for three different values of γ12 = 0, 0.1γ, 0.3γ. (c) The steady state of ρ33, and (d) the probe transmission T for three different values of γ12 = 0, 0.1γ, 0.3γ. The Rabi frequencies have been considered as Ωc(p) = 0.4γ, and the coupling laser detuning is ∆c = 0.

FIG. 5. (Color online) The probe transmission versus δ/γ in the absence of any noises and dephasing (γ12 = 0), (a) for three different values of Rabi frequencies Ωc(p) = 0.2γ, 0.4γ, 0.6γ at ∆c = 0, and (b) for three different values ∆c = 0, 0.2γ, 0.5γ at Ωc(p) = 0.4γ. (c) and (d) for three different values of Doppler width D = 0.1γ, 0.3γ, 0.5γ for Ωc(p) = 0.4γ with ∆c = 0. In (c) the two beams are copropagating and in (d) they are counterpropagating.
